title: Kernel Conscience: architecture & seq-len aware kernel optimizer for prefill/decode
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Goal: Implement a lightweight, low-latency 'kernel conscience' component in the serving runtime that selects kernels per-request using architecture (GPU type), sequence-length distribution, and attention pattern signals. The component should: 1) improve p50/p99 latency and tokens/sec for mixed prefill/decode workloads, 2) reduce per-token cost by choosing quantized or sparse-friendly kernels when safe, and 3) provide safe fallbacks and rollback hooks for regressions.

Motivation: Our current static kernel routing uses coarse rules that underperform on mixed workloads where prefill and decode have different compute/latency trade-offs. We need a per-request heuristic that is cheap to evaluate, warmstarts from microbench fingerprints, and integrates with existing KV/prefix caching and batching logic.

Scope: prototype in C++ runtime with a feature-flag rollout to canary nodes, telemetry and microbenchmark harness, and a follow-up rollout plan for dedicated pools. Excludes model compilation changes or new CUDA kernels — this work focuses on selection heuristics, telemetry, and safe rollout mechanics.
acceptance_criteria:
- New kernel selector runs <200us on p3/4-class nodes when evaluated in-path.
- End-to-end on canary traffic: p50 latency improves by >=5% and p99 does not regress by >2%.
- Tokens/sec increases by >=3% on mixed prefill/decode workloads in the microbenchmark harness.
- Observability: per-request decision reasons are emitted (kernel_id, expected_cost_score, seq_len_bucket, arch_id).
- Fallback: automatic rollback triggers on sustained 3x error-rate increase or 10% p99 regression during canary.
- Tests: unit tests for selector logic, integration test in simulation mode with synthetic traces.
design_notes:
We debated two high-level approaches: (A) heavyweight Bayesian cost model trained on microbenchmarks, (B) lightweight contextual bandit that uses runtime features and online rewards. Trade-offs: Bayesian gives better asymptotic accuracy but requires richer priors and infra; bandit is simpler and safer for incremental rollout. Decided to start with a contextual bandit guided by a deterministic fallback policy and periodic offline re-fitting.

Key features used as context: GPU architecture family, model param bucket, seq_len bucket (prefill vs decode), token phase (first-k decode vs steady-state), kv-cache hit flag, and recent batch occupancy. Warmstart strategy: map a node+model fingerprint to previously recorded microbench results in the catalogue. If no match, use conservative low-cost kernel (prefill-optimized) for first N requests and probe alternatives asynchronously.

Safety: decisions are constrained by a safety table (kernel compatibility and memory headroom). No selection that would exceed memory limits is allowed in-path.
implementation_plan:
1) Add lightweight decision API in runtime (C++): evaluate_features(), select_kernel(), emit_decision(). 2) Microbench harness: extend existing microbench to produce small fingerprint files and cost estimates for candidate kernels across seq-len buckets. 3) Implement bandit learner service (Python prototype) that consumes telemetry and updates a compact policy blob. 4) Runtime rollout: feature flag -> internal canary -> gradual percent rollout with automatic guardrails. 5) Dashboard and alerts for rollout metrics.

Milestones: Week 1 prototype selector + unit tests; Week 2 microbench + warmstart; Week 3 canary rollout; Week 4 collect data and iterate.
experiments: Compare contextual bandit vs static heuristic on synthetic mixes (prefill-heavy, decode-heavy, bimodal).
Ablation: remove seq_len bucket to measure importance of length-awareness.
Probe schedule: aggressive (probes every 100 requests) vs conservative (1 probe per 1000) to measure regret and cold-start cost.
progress_updates: 2026-01-11: Kickoff meeting with runtime, infra, and product. Agreed on bandit-first approach. (Notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Kernel+Conscience+Kickoff)
2026-01-15: Prototype evaluate_features() and select_kernel() implemented as in-memory policy in runtime; added unit tests. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4121
2026-01-20: Extended microbench harness to emit fingerprint.csv for (model, arch, seq_len) tuples. Microbench PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/microbench/pull/178

2026-01-25: Initial canary deploy on internal cluster with 5 nodes. Observed p50 improvement ~6% on internal docs generation workload; p99 stable. Telemetry dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/KernelConscience/canary-01

2026-01-28: Discovered higher tail latency when probes coincided with large decode batches. Mitigation: add probe-suppression during high occupancy windows and limit async probe concurrency. Implemented patch PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4203

2026-02-02: Ongoing: collecting 2 weeks of telemetry; preparing safety tests and integration test for fallback. Blocker: need updated kernel compatibility table from kernel-team (request sent, tracking: KERNEL-REQ-2026-04).
